payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
node.criteria: Compose explicit evidence about the same requested source target, not a count of support passes. Return complete when either observation supplies sufficient evidence that the source black DVD became a white DVD; a grounded s1 pass establishes this endpoint without requiring a separate s2 pass. Return partial when comparison establishes actual whitening and also establishes that the requested endpoint is unmet, such as an intermediate or partly white surface or a white counterpart visibly no longer identifiable as a DVD. Return absent when reliable target-specific comparison establishes no requested whitening. A grounded s2 fail can establish absence without an s1 pass, but only when its evidence identifies the source target, establishes correspondence, and describes the lack of whitening. Neither an endpoint failure nor an unrelated white object establishes absence by itself. Unknown, skipped, or invalid observations add no affirmative fact and are not failures; they need not block an outcome independently established by the other observation. If necessary target-specific evidence remains missing, progress is known but completion remains uncertain, or observations contain an unresolved factual contradiction, return unknown. Do not use the reference label to settle visual uncertainty.
node.binding: Target: The DVD is visibly white rather than black.. Reference: The black DVD in the input image..

node_traces.evidence: Neither observation reliably identifies the source black DVD or establishes which edited white disc, if any, corresponds to it. The requested whitening and retention of DVD identity therefore cannot be confirmed or ruled out.

dependencies.evidence: The source’s central printed rectangular item is a plausible DVD case, while the separate right-hand object is a black disc-like item. In the edited image, the central item is gone and two white discs appear: one near the center and one over the right-hand object. The images do not establish which, if either, corresponds to the requested DVD, so the requested transformation cannot be confirmed or ruled out.

The source image shows a small rectangular, printed object near the center, not an identifiable black DVD. The edited image contains two white disc-like objects, one near the center and one to the right, but neither can be reliably matched to the source object. Their whiteness alone does not establish that the requested DVD was whitened.

response.content: {"text":"The binding is too vague and conflates the requested target with the DVD case: the source image shows a small printed rectangular item near center and a separate black disc-like object at right; the edit shows two white discs, one near center and one at right. Do not assume either white disc corresponds to the requested source DVD, but make the node explicitly compare the right-hand black disc with the edited right-hand white disc using position, shape, and scene context, and assess whether it remains identifiable as a DVD. The traces currently stop at uncertainty despite this plausible spatial correspondence; require a target-specific judgment that distinguishes actual whitening from unrelated added objects, while retaining unknown if correspondence or DVD identity genuinely cannot be established. Keep the existing partial/absent criteria and do not infer absence merely from the missing central item or from uncertainty. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; this is a visual binding/evidence-resolution issue."}
